original_benchmark.notes: Dual-axis observation-contract benchmark. 33 tasks where an LLM agent interacts with a local FastAPI server and must preserve API contracts along two axes: validity and integrity. The original harness ships one agent: a native OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini tool-calling loop with a single bash tool (agents/docker_runner.py), versioned here by the harness commit used for parity.

harbor_adapter.notes: Adapter copies the 33 upstream harbor/cookbook-export tasks and applies the documented changes (canary strip, benchmark-name scrub, trusted grading helper in tests/, task server in a separate task-server compose service, separate verifier container fed by collected artifacts, version 1.0 and author credits in task.toml); server behaviour and scoring logic are unchanged. Parity uses contractbench-parity-agent@1.0.0, a Harbor port of the original harness's tool-calling loop (Scenario 3). Standard-agent run on the same tasks (generalization, not parity): mini-swe-agent@2.4.6 with gpt-4o-2024-08-06, temperature 0.0, step_limit 30, 1 run: mean reward 34.22%, pass rate 28.12% over 32 scored tasks (1 trial lost to a container-setup network error), cost $11.11. parity_costs covers the parity experiment only: original side about $22 (list price from logged token counts) plus Harbor side $15.49 (sanity check, 3 runs and the 3 rerun trials, from recorded usage).
